code_analysis_guide.overview: Systematic approach to static code analysis for identifying software defects, anti-patterns, and misconfigurations that contribute to production incidents. This guide focuses on reliability, performance, and operational issues that manifest as observable symptoms in Instana and OpenShift.

category.name: error_handling
category.description: Examine how the application handles errors, exceptions, and failure scenarios

anti_pattern.name: swallowed_exceptions
anti_pattern.description: Catching exceptions without logging or handling
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Silent failures in Instana traces - Missing error context in logs - Difficult to diagnose issues

anti_pattern.name: generic_exception_catching
anti_pattern.description: Catching overly broad exception types
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Masking specific errors - Incorrect error handling - Loss of error context

anti_pattern.name: missing_error_propagation
anti_pattern.description: Not propagating errors to callers
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Partial failures not visible - Inconsistent state - Difficult debugging

anti_pattern.name: missing_timeout_handling
anti_pattern.description: No timeout configuration for external calls
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Thread exhaustion in Instana - Hanging requests - Cascading failures

code_examples.good: HttpClient client = HttpClient.newBuilder() .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5)) .build(); HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder() .uri(uri) .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)) .build();

checklist.item: Are all exceptions logged with context?
Are specific exception types caught rather than generic Exception?
Are errors propagated to callers appropriately?
Are timeouts configured for all external calls?
Are retry mechanisms implemented safely?
Are circuit breakers in place for external dependencies?

category.name: resource_management
category.description: Examine how the application manages resources (connections, memory, threads, files)

anti_pattern.name: connection_leaks
anti_pattern.description: Not closing database connections or HTTP clients
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Connection pool exhaustion in Instana - "Too many connections" errors in logs - Increasing connection count over time

anti_pattern.name: memory_leaks
anti_pattern.description: Unbounded caches, collections, or listeners
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Increasing heap usage in Instana - OOMKilled pods in OpenShift - Frequent GC pauses

anti_pattern.name: thread_pool_exhaustion
anti_pattern.description: Creating threads without limits or using unbounded executors
anti_pattern.symptoms: - High thread count in Instana - CPU saturation - OutOfMemoryError: unable to create new native thread

code_examples.bad: ExecutorService executor = Executors.newCachedThreadPool(); // Unbounded thread pool, can create unlimited threads
code_examples.good: ExecutorService executor = new ThreadPoolExecutor( 10, // core pool size 50, // maximum pool size 60L, TimeUnit.SECONDS, new LinkedBlockingQueue<>(1000), // bounded queue new ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy() // rejection policy );

anti_pattern.name: file_handle_leaks
anti_pattern.description: Not closing file streams or readers
anti_pattern.symptoms: - "Too many open files" errors - File descriptor exhaustion - Application hangs

checklist.item: Are all resources (connections, streams, readers) closed properly?
Is try-with-resources used for AutoCloseable resources?
Are caches bounded with eviction policies?
Are thread pools configured with appropriate limits?
Are there any static collections that grow unbounded?
Is memory usage monitored and managed?

category.name: database_interactions
category.description: Examine database queries, connection management, and transaction handling

anti_pattern.name: n_plus_one_queries
anti_pattern.description: Executing N queries in a loop instead of one query
anti_pattern.symptoms: - High database call count in Instana - Slow endpoint latency - Database connection pool exhaustion

code_examples.good: List<Order> orders = orderRepository.findAllWithCustomers(); // Single query with JOIN to fetch orders and customers

anti_pattern.name: missing_indexes
anti_pattern.description: Queries on unindexed columns
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Slow query warnings in logs - High database CPU in Instana - Increasing query latency
anti_pattern.detection: - Look for WHERE clauses on columns without indexes - Check for queries on large tables without indexes - Review database slow query logs

anti_pattern.name: large_result_sets
anti_pattern.description: Loading large result sets without pagination
anti_pattern.symptoms: - High memory usage - OOMKilled pods - Slow response times

code_examples.bad: List<Order> orders = orderRepository.findAll(); // Loads all orders into memory

anti_pattern.name: long_transactions
anti_pattern.description: Transactions held open for too long
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Database lock contention - Deadlocks - Slow transaction commits

anti_pattern.name: connection_pool_misconfiguration
anti_pattern.description: Connection pool size too small or too large
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Connection timeout errors - "Waiting for connection" messages - Database connection exhaustion

checklist.item: Are queries optimized to avoid N+1 problems?
Are appropriate indexes defined for query patterns?
Is pagination used for large result sets?
Are transactions kept short and focused?
Is connection pool properly configured?
Are prepared statements used to prevent SQL injection?

category.name: concurrency_issues
category.description: Examine thread safety, synchronization, and concurrent access patterns

anti_pattern.name: race_conditions
anti_pattern.description: Unsynchronized access to shared mutable state
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Intermittent data corruption - Inconsistent state - Hard-to-reproduce bugs

anti_pattern.name: deadlocks
anti_pattern.description: Circular lock dependencies
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Application hangs - Threads blocked indefinitely - Thread dumps show circular waits

anti_pattern.name: blocking_on_event_loop
anti_pattern.description: Blocking operations on async/reactive event loops
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Thread starvation - Poor throughput - High latency

anti_pattern.name: improper_locking
anti_pattern.description: Locks held too long or too coarse-grained
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Lock contention - Poor concurrency - Reduced throughput

checklist.item: Is shared mutable state properly synchronized?
Are thread-safe collections used where appropriate?
Are locks acquired in consistent order to prevent deadlocks?
Are blocking operations moved off event loop threads?
Are locks held for minimal time?
Are immutable objects used where possible?

category.name: configuration_issues
category.description: Examine application configuration, environment variables, and settings

anti_pattern.name: hardcoded_values
anti_pattern.description: Configuration values hardcoded instead of externalized
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Different behavior across environments - Difficult to change settings - Requires code changes for config updates

code_examples.bad: private static final String API_URL = "https://api.production.com"; private static final int TIMEOUT = 5000;

anti_pattern.name: missing_environment_validation
anti_pattern.description: Not validating required configuration at startup
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Runtime failures due to missing config - Pods crash after deployment - Difficult to diagnose config issues

anti_pattern.name: incorrect_resource_limits
anti_pattern.description: JVM heap size or other limits not matching container limits
anti_pattern.symptoms: - OOMKilled despite available memory - Poor GC performance - Inefficient resource usage

configuration_checks.check: JVM -Xmx should be ~75% of container memory limit
Thread pool sizes appropriate for CPU limits
Connection pool sizes appropriate for load

anti_pattern.name: missing_retry_configuration
anti_pattern.description: No retry logic or exponential backoff for transient failures
anti_pattern.symptoms: - Failures on transient errors - Retry storms amplifying issues - Cascading failures

checklist.item: Are all configuration values externalized?
Is required configuration validated at startup?
Are resource limits (heap, threads, connections) properly configured?
Are retry policies configured with exponential backoff?
Are circuit breakers configured for external dependencies?
Are timeouts configured for all external calls?

category.name: dependency_management
category.description: Examine dependency versions, compatibility, and security vulnerabilities

check.name: version_conflicts
check.look_for: - Multiple versions of same library - Incompatible version combinations - Transitive dependency conflicts

check.name: outdated_dependencies
check.description: Check for outdated or vulnerable dependencies
check.symptoms: - Known security vulnerabilities - Missing bug fixes - Compatibility issues
check.tools: - Maven: mvn versions:display-dependency-updates - Gradle: gradle dependencyUpdates - npm: npm outdated

check.name: missing_dependencies
check.symptoms: - ClassNotFoundException at runtime - NoClassDefFoundError - Module not found errors

step.title: Identify code areas from Instana traces

actions.action: Extract service names and endpoints from Instana errors
Identify slow spans and their associated code paths
Note specific error messages and stack traces

tools.tool: search_files with error messages or class names

step.title: Read and analyze code
step.focus_areas: - Error handling in the problematic code path - Resource management (connections, streams) - Database queries and transactions - External API calls and timeouts - Configuration usage

step.title: Check configuration files
step.files_to_examine: - application.properties / application.yml - ConfigMaps (from OpenShift) - Environment variables - Database connection settings - Thread pool configurations

correlation_checks.check: Does missing timeout explain connection hangs in Instana?
Does unbounded cache explain OOMKills in OpenShift?
Does N+1 query explain high database calls in Instana?
Does missing error handling explain silent failures?

guideline.name: cite_specific_locations
guideline.description: Always provide exact file paths and line numbers for issues found
guideline.example: Found connection leak in src/main/java/com/example/PaymentService.java:45 where Connection is obtained but not closed in finally block.

guideline.name: include_code_snippets
guideline.description: Include the problematic code snippet in the RCA report
guideline.format: Use code blocks with syntax highlighting and line numbers

guideline.name: explain_impact
guideline.description: Explain how the code issue leads to the observed symptoms
guideline.example: The missing connection.close() in the finally block causes connections to leak. Over time, this exhausts the connection pool (max 20 connections), leading to "Timeout waiting for connection" errors seen in Instana traces and "Too many connections" errors in pod logs.

guideline.name: provide_fix
guideline.description: Provide specific code changes needed to fix the issue
guideline.format: Show before/after code or provide exact changes using apply_diff format

practice.title: Focus on reliability patterns
practice.description: Prioritize issues that affect reliability: error handling, resource management, timeouts, retries, circuit breakers

practice.title: Look for correlation with symptoms
practice.description: Don't just list code issues - explain how they cause the observed problems in Instana and OpenShift

practice.title: Check recent changes
practice.description: If incident followed a deployment, focus on recently changed code using git diff or deployment history

practice.title: Validate configuration
practice.description: Always check that configuration values (timeouts, pool sizes, limits) are appropriate for the environment and load

practice.title: Consider the full request path
practice.description: Trace the request path from entry point through all layers (controller → service → repository → database) to find issues
